title: The Joint Custody
logline: Wendy the Waitress quits MacLaren's after eleven years to open Overheard, a bar built from everything the gang ever said in the booth, with a perk eerily tailored to each of them. Marshall drafts a joint custody agreement between the two bars, Ted boycotts for the sake of the sacred booth, Barney weighs his legendary tab against a zero-percent transfer, and Carl finally leaves the bar to say more than one word.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2012, all five of us became children of divorce. For me, it was the second time.

couch.line: Wait. Aunt Lily and Uncle Marshall got divorced?
What? No. Worse. Wendy the waitress quit MacLaren's.
That's not a divorce. That's a job.
Luke, there was a custody agreement. It was eleven pages.

guests.name: Leonard Pfaff
guests.role: An actuary who wandered into Overheard on opening night and keeps coming back. Every dish on the menu is named after one of the gang, so he knows far too much about five strangers, and he reports all of it in a flat monotone.

scenes.summary: Wendy brings the usual round and her two weeks' notice: she's opening Overheard around the corner, built from eleven years of eavesdropping, and wants the gang as her first regulars. Ted refuses on behalf of the sacred, imperfect booth; Barney can't abandon his eleven-year tab (cutaway: how he pictures Carl and their little leather book). Carl: 'Good for her.' The gang swears loyalty, then admits they opened their tailored invitations eight seconds earlier. Barney's invitation offers to refinance him.

beats.line: It was a Tuesday. Wendy brought our usual round, the way she had for eleven years.
Two beers, a white wine, two scotches, and my two weeks' notice.
You're quitting? Wendy, you can't quit. You're load-bearing.
I'm opening my own bar. Right around the corner. It's called Overheard.
Overheard. Why Overheard?
Eleven years, you all talked in front of me like I was furniture. Turns out furniture takes notes.
I've saved every tip since 2001. Barney tips a twenty every time he lies to a woman.
So you're a millionaire.
And Ted, you've said we should open a bar forty-one times. I'm the one who did it.
Forty-one? I've said it maybe twice.
March ninth, 2009. Nine-forty. Second beer. Guys, we should open a bar with a really good coat check.
It's an underserved market!
I want you five to be my first regulars. I built every inch of it for you.
Wendy, we're honored. But we can't. This booth is sacred.
The table's two inches too low. The lamp hums in B flat. That bench has a spring that's been stabbing Marshall since 2005.
Every single night, Wendy. And I have never once complained.
Out loud.
I know, Ted. I wrote down every complaint you ever made. I built a whole bar out of them.
You built a bar out of my complaints?
It took a while. There were a lot.
Well, I can't leave either. I have a tab here. Eleven years. Never once closed.
Carl and I have something special, Wendy. It's called debt.
The one commitment you've ever made, and it's to not paying.
A tab isn't a debt, Robin. It's a promise that you're coming back. Every night, Carl writes my drinks in our little leather book.
Another scotch, Carl. Put it on the tab.
You got it, buddy. Going in our book.
Our book.
Some nights I read it after closing. Just to feel close to you.
Barney, Carl has never said buddy in his life.
Nope.
Opening night is Thursday. There's an invitation for each of you. Every one is a little tailored.
Don't open them in here. Carl reads lips.
Carl! Did you hear that? Wendy's leaving!
Yep.
Eleven years, and that's all you've got? Yep?
Good for her.
Okay. Nobody goes to that bar. We are MacLaren's people. Swear it.
We swear.
Lily. Mine has a picture of a cheese curd.
Mine says solo show.
Mine says Canadian feed.
You opened them? We swore four seconds ago!
We opened them eight seconds ago.
Ted. Mine says zero percent interest for eighteen months.
She wants to refinance me.

scenes.summary: Overheard, opening night. Marshall's curds still squeak (a guy on a plane), Lily's portfolio from 2008 is a solo show (kept for leverage), Robin has the Canadian feed and a very sad loon, and the house rules know about the mall. Leonard, the lone stranger, has eaten 'the Marshall' four times. Ted and Barney arrive to retrieve the traitors. Barney comes for the zero-percent tab transfer; Ted is ambushed by a thirty-inch table and a lamp in A, and calls it a trap. Marshall proposes joint custody. Ted storms out, then comes back nine seconds later for curds to go. For Carl.

beats.line: Kids, our sacred oath lasted until Thursday. About seven-oh-five.
Lily, they squeak. A cheese curd stops squeaking twelve hours after it's made.
Wendy has a guy on a plane.
Gunnar. He flies in from St. Cloud every morning. He thinks it's for a hospital.
Wendy, these are my paintings. On every wall. How?
You left your portfolio in the booth. September twelfth, 2008. I kept it.
For safekeeping?
For leverage.
That's exactly what I would've done. Marshall, I think I'm in love with her.
She got me the Canadian feed. There's a commercial about a lonely loon looking for his flock.
She cried.
I did not cry. It was a very sad loon.
Rule two. Nobody mentions the mall.
beats.title: Overheard: House Rules

beats.line: Wendy. How do you know about the mall?
Robin. Everybody knows about the mall.
Excuse me. Do you have anything that isn't named after one of them?
I've had the Marshall four times. I still don't know who Marshall is.
I'm Marshall!
You're bigger than the sandwich. Not by much.
I knew it!
Two days after a sacred oath, and you're eating curds in the enemy camp.
Ted, they squeak.
Robin?
Loon.
Barney. Back me up.
I'm not a customer, Ted. I'm here for the paperwork.
Your MacLaren's tab, transferred here. Zero percent for eighteen months. I just need the balance from Carl.
Easy. Carl writes down every drink. Ted, do you know how many scotches fit in eighteen months?
Two thousand one hundred and ninety. I did the math. For you.
And Ted. Before you yell. Your table.
Thirty inches.
Oh no. My knees feel respected.
Wait. Is that lamp humming in A?
You said B flat was the key of regret. October 2010. The week after the wedding thing.
No. This is a trap. A beautiful, ergonomically correct trap.
Ted, it's two bars. We don't have to pick. Kids do this all the time.
Joint custody! I'll draft it tonight. MacLaren's gets Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Overheard gets Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Who gets Christmas?
Whoever has the Canadian feed.
Done.
I'm not signing. I've been through one divorce. My parents told me at brunch. A year late.
I still can't look at a mimosa.
Barney. We're leaving.
You go ahead. I'll catch up in eighteen months.
Fine. Enjoy your perfect bar. I'll be at the imperfect one. Where we belong.
He'll be back. Ted has stormed out of a hundred and four places. Average return, nine seconds.
Could I get some curds to go? For Carl.
So that was Ted. I've had his salad. It comes with a pamphlet.

scenes.summary: The custody agreement takes effect (eleven pages, section eleven covers Arbor Day). Wednesday, MacLaren's night: Lily, Marshall and Robin act like kids at Dad's (Wendy lets us have nachos for dinner), and Marshall greets his spring. Barney asks Carl for his balance: Carl never wrote it down. There is no book. Barney storms off to a bar that writes things down. The others invoke section nine, emergency curds. Alone with Carl, Ted says what MacLaren's is to him; Carl says 'Yep', then walks out from behind the bar. Ted: 'You have an out?'

beats.line: Marshall's custody agreement took effect that Monday.
Section eleven covered Arbor Day.
beats.title: Joint Custody Agreement
lines: Christmas: whoever has the Canadian feed

beats.line: Wednesday! MacLaren's night! Welcome home, guys.
Hi, Carl.
Hi.
At Wendy's, they say hi with our names.
Carl, can we have nachos for dinner?
No.
Wendy lets us have nachos for dinner.
Do you hear yourselves? You sound like children of divorce. I was one for a year before anybody told me.
Ow.
Hi, buddy. I missed you too.
Carl! Big night. Wendy's transferring my tab. I just need the balance.
What tab?
My tab! Eleven years! You write it in our little leather book!
Never wrote it down.
And the book?
What book?
Ted. Was any of it real?
Barney, he's given you free drinks for eleven years. That's the nicest thing anyone's ever done for you.
Free? I've been ordering the cheap scotch to keep the bill down!
I'm going to Overheard. Where they write things down.
Ted, the loon commercial's on at ten. Tonight he finds his flock.
And Wendy's hosting an artist talk. By me. About me.
And the curd plane landed early. Ted, we're invoking section nine. Emergency curds.
That is not what section nine is for!
Ted, I wrote section nine.
Just us now, Carl. The loyal ones.
I'm working.
You know what this place is, Carl? Every bad date I ever had, I came here after.
Every good one too. Nobody designed it for us. It was just always here.
Yep.
Doesn't it bother you? They're over there. Wendy's over there.
Carl? Where are you going?
Out.
You have an out?

scenes.summary: Overheard, same night. Barney wants a real tab, written in ink; Wendy confesses opening week was thirty-seven gang visits and four Leonards: she built a perfect bar for five people. Carl walks in (Carl has legs), Ted right behind him: Carl is Wendy's silent partner, so the loyal move all week was drinking here, and Ted ate Carl's curds. Carl remembers the exact minute Wendy asked him how to run a bar, then gives the longest speech of his life: you don't build a bar for regulars, you open the door and wait until they're family. That's why he never wrote down Barney's tab. Barney switches to the good scotch, retroactively. Wendy drops the tailoring, keeps her nerve, and gets asked her first question in eleven years. Ted sits at the thirty-inch table; Carl says the MacLaren's table stays two inches too low.

beats.line: Wendy! Open me a tab. A real one. Write everything down. In ink.
Barney, I'd love to. But I need at least one customer who actually pays.
What are you talking about? This place is a hit.
Opening week, I had forty-one customers. Thirty-seven were you five.
Four were me.
I built the perfect bar for five people. Turns out that's a bar for five people.
Then we'll come every night. Forget the custody agreement.
Lily! Section two! No speaking ill of either bar in front of the other bar!
Carl? Outside? In the wild?
I always assumed he was bolted to the floor.
Carl! You too? I boycotted this place for you!
Ted. Carl's my silent partner. He put up half the money.
Carl, you're silent everything.
So all week, the loyal thing to do was drink here?
Yep.
Never got my curds.
They were losing their squeak, Carl!
Carl, I'm sorry. Eleven years of listening, and I still built it wrong.
April third, 2001. Eight-oh-five. You walked in and asked me how to run a bar.
You remember the time?
I listen too.
I told you, learn the regulars. You learned them better than anybody I ever hired.
But you built a bar for five people. Those five already have a bar. They never leave. They tip in nachos.
You don't build a bar for regulars, Wendy. You open the door. You pour. You wait.
One day you look up, and they're family. That's all MacLaren's ever was. A room that waited.
Carl. Is that why you never wrote down my tab?
Don't charge family.
Then I'm switching to the good scotch. Retroactively.
Carl, that's the most you've ever said.
Ninety-five words. I need to sit down.
Okay. New plan. No more curd planes. No more house rules. No more tailoring.
Not the loon.
Fine. But my paintings stay. I know where you live, Wendy.
Lily, I know where you've lived since 2001.
So what do you want Overheard to be, Wendy?
Ted. That's the first question any of you has ever asked me.
That's not true. We ask you things all the time!
Can we get another round doesn't count.
A bar where people tell me things on purpose.
Leonard. Tomorrow there's a sandwich with your name on it. Tell me about yourself.
Nobody's asked me that since 1987.
For the record, Carl, the table at MacLaren's is still two inches too low.
Staying that way.
Kids, I told you we became children of divorce. Turns out Mom and Dad were business partners the whole time.
So we did what children of divorce do best. We milked it. Barney hasn't paid for a drink since.
